title: Low-cost tissue collection and genomic DNA extraction for plants
author: Rachel A Howard-Till
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdg9i3z6
materials: Grind dry tissue to a fine powder.
Clear lysate and bind DNA to silica matrix.

steps.title: Collect and desiccate plant tissues
steps.instruction: Collect plant tissue and place in a sealed container with silica gel orange (or equivalent).

substeps.instruction: For larger samples (e.g., Berberis darwinii), place approximately 30 leaves in a 50 ml falcon tube; fill tubes partially, shake to distribute leaves, then fill the remaining space with silica.

For smaller amounts or soft leaves, place tissue in eppendorf tubes (filled and capped with silica) or place open tubes in a box inside a sealable container, cover with breathable material (e.g., cheesecloth or disposable cleaning cloth), and layer silica gel over the cloth.
Incubate Berberis tissue in silica for at least 4 days at room temperature.
Incubate soft tissue in silica for 2 days at room temperature.
Verify tissue is brittle and breaks when pinched; if soft, incubate longer. Replace saturated silica gel if the color indicator changes.

steps.title: Grind plant tissue
steps.instruction: Mechanically grind the desiccated tissue into a fine powder using a tissue homogenizer or alternative method.

substeps.instruction: For Berberis: Place ~100 mg of dry tissue (7 leaves) in a 7 ml screw cap tube with six 2.8 mm and two 5.0 mm ceramic beads. Grind using a Precellys Evolution tissue homogenizer with 3 pulses of 20 seconds at 4500 rpm.
For softer tissue (e.g., L. luteus, Camelina sativa, or flax): Place in 2 ml screw cap tubes with three 2.8 mm ceramic beads and grind once for 20 seconds at 4500 rpm.
Alternative: Use manual grinding with mortar and pestle, or in-tube grinding with sand, glass, or metal beads on a lab vortexer.

steps.title: Prepare binding buffer and silica matrix
steps.instruction: Prepare tubes containing the binding matrix (can be done in advance).

substeps.instruction: Combine 50 µL SILICA slurry and 700 µL BINDING buffer (2 M guanidine thiocyanate in 67% EtOH final concentrations) in a 2 ml eppendorf tube.
Prepare one tube for each 2 ml lysis tube, or 3 tubes for each 7 ml lysis tube.

steps.title: Lyse tissue and remove RNA
steps.instruction: Add lysis buffer containing RNase to the ground tissue and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare LYSIS BUFFER (0.5% SDS, 10 mM EDTA, 2.5 µg/ml RNase).
For 7 ml tubes: Add 2.4 mL LYSIS buffer.
For 2 ml tubes: Add 800 µL LYSIS buffer.
Shake or vortex tubes for 2 minutes to completely suspend tissue.
Incubate tubes for 10 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Add sodium acetate to the lysate and incubate on ice.

substeps.instruction: Add 600 µL 3M Na Acetate for 7 ml tubes, or 200 µL 3M Na Acetate for 2 ml tubes.
Mix well and incubate for 5 minutes on ice.
If using 7 ml tubes, distribute the lysate slurry into 3 eppendorf tubes.

steps.title: Clear lysate and bind DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate and bind the DNA to the silica matrix.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes for 3 minutes at 13000 rpm at room temperature to clear lysate.
Transfer lysate (~800 µL) to the prepared tubes containing BINDING BUFFER and SILICA.
Flick or vortex to resuspend silica.
Incubate tubes for 45 to 90 minutes at 4 °C.
Shake on a multivortexer for 15 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash DNA-bound silica pellets
steps.instruction: Wash the silica pellets to remove impurities.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13000 rpm for 3 minutes at room temperature and discard the supernatant.
Add 500 µL WASH buffer, flick or vortex to resuspend silica.
Centrifuge at 13000 rpm for 3 minutes at room temperature and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the wash step two more times (total of 3 washes).
Invert tubes on paper towels and tap gently to remove remaining liquid.
Leave tubes open on their sides to dry pellets completely for approximately 1.5 hours at room temperature.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Elute the DNA from the silica pellet using TE buffer and RNase.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL TE + 12.5 ug/ml RNase A to the pellet and flick to resuspend.
Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature while shaking at low speed.
Centrifuge at 13000 rpm for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Pipette the supernatant into a fresh 1.5 ml eppendorf tube.
For maximum yield, repeat the elution and combine the second eluant with the first.

steps.title: Final RNA removal and concentration
steps.instruction: Perform final purification and optional concentration of the DNA.

substeps.instruction: To ensure complete RNA removal, incubate DNA overnight at 4 °C.
To concentrate DNA and remove protein impurities, perform PEG precipitation: use a final concentration of 13.3% PEG 6000 and 10 mM MgCl2.
Incubate PEG mixture for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 13000 rpm for 10 minutes.
